# puzzlekit

> Small helpers for puzzle code: search over implicit state spaces, integer grids, input
> parsing. Python 3.13+, no runtime dependencies. Extracted from a review of ~44 Advent
> of Code and Google Foobar solutions, so each function exists because the same shape was
> rewritten — often differently, sometimes wrongly — in file after file.

Key API decisions, because they are unusual on purpose:

- `explore(starts, succ, *, order, key=identity)` takes a successor **function**, not a
  materialised graph. `order` is `"fifo"`, `"lifo"` or `"priority"` and has **no
  default**: `"lifo"` with a visited set is component labelling, `"fifo"` is
  shortest-path, and confusing them is a silent wrong answer.
- `key` sets the deduplication identity. `key=None` disables dedup entirely, which is
  required for counting paths rather than states. `order="priority"` with `key=None`
  raises.
- `succ(state)` yields `(next_state, step_cost)` and owns all domain rules: bounds,
  walls, turn costs.
- `dijkstra` returns `(dist, preds)` with every optimal predecessor; `backtrack(preds,
  targets)` recovers all shortest paths without a second traversal.
- `Grid[p]` raises off-grid rather than wrapping like a list. `Grid.get(p, "#")` is the
  bounds-checked fetch. `Grid.neighbors` yields `(delta, position, value)`.
- `Vec` is `(row, col)` with row increasing downwards; `rot(1)` is clockwise;
  `norm2()` returns an exact `int`.
- `ints(s)` returns every integer in a string; `sections(s)` splits on blank lines.

Deliberately not provided, with the recommended alternative: union-find
(`scipy.cluster.hierarchy.DisjointSet`), integer infinity (`sys.maxsize`), popcount
(`int.bit_count`), flood fill and neighbour counts (`scipy.ndimage.label`,
`scipy.ndimage.convolve`), sentinel borders (`numpy.pad`), sliding windows
(`numpy.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view`), Dijkstra on explicit graphs
(`scipy.sparse.csgraph`, `networkx`), topological order (`graphlib.TopologicalSorter`),
memoization (`functools.cache`), puzzle input fetching (`aocd`).

## Docs

- [Search](https://bur.gy/puzzlekit/searching.html): `explore`, `dijkstra`, `backtrack`; why `order` has no default; when not to use a frontier at all
- [Grids and vectors](https://bur.gy/puzzlekit/grid.html): `Grid`, `Vec`, `ray`, and when to reach for numpy/scipy instead
- [Parsing and bits](https://bur.gy/puzzlekit/parsing.html): `ints`, `sections`, `text`, `lines`, `bits`
- [Design notes](https://bur.gy/puzzlekit/design.html): the review findings behind each API decision, and the three modules that were cut because they already existed
- [API reference](https://bur.gy/puzzlekit/api.html): full signatures and docstrings

## Optional

- [Source](https://github.com/jburgy/puzzlekit): implementation and tests
- [Examples](https://github.com/jburgy/puzzlekit/tree/main/examples): runnable solutions that assert their own answers
- [Originating code review](https://github.com/jburgy/blog/blob/main/CODE_REVIEW.md): the full write-up this package was extracted from
